question: According to the World Spider Catalog, which spiders of the family Desidae and genus Desis are native to one country. Provide their full scientific names and the location they are indigenous to.
gold_answer: Desis bobmarleyi - Endemic to Australia (specifically Queensland), Desis galapagoensis - Endemic to the Galapagos Islands (Ecuador), Desis gardineri - Endemic to the Laccadive Islands (India), Desis inermis - Endemic to India, Desis japonica - Endemic to Japan, Desis jiaxiangi - Endemic to China, Desis kenyonae - Endemic to Australia (specifically Victoria and Tasmania), Desis vorax - Endemic to Samoa, Desis risbeci - Endemic to New Caledonia

answer:
**Desis species (family Desidae) that are native to only one country (according to the World Spider Catalog)**  

| Scientific name | Country where the species is indigenous | Notes |
|------------------|----------------------------------------|-------|
| *Desis bobmarleyi* Baehr, Raven & Harms, 2017 | Australia (Queensland) | The WSC lists its distribution as “Australia (Queensland)” – no other country is given. <sup>[1]</sup> |
| *Desis gardineri* Pocock, 1904 | India (Laccadive Islands) | Distribution note is “India (Laccadive Islands)”. <sup>[1]</sup> |
| *Desis inermis* Gravely, 1927 | India | WSC entry shows “India” only. <sup>[1]</sup> |
| *Desis japonica* Yaginuma, 1956 | Japan | Only “Japan” is listed in its distribution. <sup>[1]</sup> |
| *Desis jiaxiangi* Lin, Li & Chen, 2020 | China | WSC records “China” alone. <sup>[1]</sup> |
| *Desis kenyonae* Pocock, 1902 | Australia (Victoria, Tasmania) | Distribution is “Australia (Victoria, Tasmania)”. <sup>[1]</sup> |
| *Desis galapagoensis* Hirst, 1925 | Ecuador (Galápagos Islands) | The entry shows “Galápagos” – the archipelago is part of Ecuador, and no other country appears. <sup>[1]</sup> |

**Summary**

The World Spider Catalog lists seven *Desis* species whose recorded distribution is restricted to a single country (or, in the case of *Desis galapagoensis*, to the Galápagos Islands of Ecuador). All other *Desis* species in the catalog have been recorded in two or more countries, so they do not meet the “native to one country” criterion.

**Desis species (family Desidae) that are native to only one country (according to the World Spider Catalog)**  

| Scientific name | Country where the species is indigenous | Notes |
|------------------|----------------------------------------|-------|
| *Desis bobmarleyi* Baehr, Raven & Harms, 2017 | Australia (Queensland) | The WSC lists its distribution as “Australia (Queensland)” – no other country is given. <sup>[1]</sup> |
| *Desis gardineri* Pocock, 1904 | India (Laccadive Islands) | Distribution note is “India (Laccadive Islands)”. <sup>[1]</sup> |
| *Desis inermis* Gravely, 1927 | India | WSC entry shows “India” only. <sup>[1]</sup> |
| *Desis japonica* Yaginuma, 1956 | Japan | Only “Japan” is listed in its distribution. <sup>[1]</sup> |
| *Desis jiaxiangi* Lin, Li & Chen, 2020 | China | WSC records “China” alone. <sup>[1]</sup> |
| *Desis kenyonae* Pocock, 1902 | Australia (Victoria, Tasmania) | Distribution is “Australia (Victoria, Tasmania)”. <sup>[1]</sup> |
| *Desis galapagoensis* Hirst, 1925 | Ecuador (Galápagos Islands) | The entry shows “Galápagos” – the archipelago is part of Ecuador, and no other country appears. <sup>[1]</sup> |

**Summary**

The World Spider Catalog lists seven *Desis* species whose recorded distribution is restricted to a single country (or, in the case of *Desis galapagoensis*, to the Galápagos Islands of Ecuador). All other *Desis* species in the catalog have been recorded in two or more countries, so they do not meet the “native to one country” criterion.
